steps.note: the API built this case's state
Configure the event as an RFQ rather than the default auction.
Apply an RFQ pricing template before adding line items.
Create the two-line pricing sheet required by the scenario.
Complete the RFQ pricing sheet so the event can be published.
Invite one vendor for the normal vendor-side bid.
Submit a normal vendor-portal bid; the catalog applies this value to every line.
Verify the vendor bid was accepted by the portal.
Open the buyer comparison grid where the counter-offer control is available.
Send a buyer counter offer while bidding is live.
Verify the buyer grid marks the vendor bid as having a counter offer.
Switch to the vendor portal flow and accept the pending counter offer.
Verify the buyer-side response grid records the counter offer as accepted.
Return to the buyer's Responses tab for the post-acceptance response check.
Verify the buyer still sees the vendor's direct response after acceptance.
Reopen Master QCS to inspect the resulting current bid values.
Verify Master QCS recalculates each line amount and the total from the current prices.
